question.text: Kaveri Macro Fund (Cat III) delivered an annualised return of 18.4% against its benchmark (CRISIL AIF Index — Cat III) return of 12.8%. Tracking error over the same period is 4.0%. What is the Information Ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: Information Ratio = (Fund Return - Benchmark Return) / Tracking Error = (18.4% - 12.8%) / 4.0% = 5.6 / 4.0 = 1.40. IR > 1.0 is considered strong for Cat III active managers; IR > 0.5 is typically acceptable. IR differs from Sharpe in using benchmark (not risk-free) and TE (not total SD). The Trap: Option A (0.70) mistakenly subtracts the risk-free rate instead of benchmark return. Option C (2.24) divides by SD of benchmark only. Option D (4.60) is the raw active return in %. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PM), XV (RA), and X-A/B (IA) all test IR as a core active-management metric. Cat I/II (XIX-D) lean on IRR/MOIC/PME because of illiquid private cash-flows, so IR is less central there — Cat III uses IR/Sharpe/Sortino as primary performance metrics. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat III LPs increasingly ask for IR on a rolling 36-month basis — not lifetime — because short-lived alpha from a single regime (e.g., 2020 vol spike) can inflate lifetime IR. Track rolling IR quarterly for investor letters.
